b1-unit-07.07.1 Danny's job interview:
Interviewer: Hello Danny, come in. Please have a seat. I'm Carla, the manager of City Steps Tours.
Danny: Hi, nice to meet you. Thanks for inviting me.
Interviewer: So, tell me a little about yourself.
Danny: Sure. I'm from Chicago, and I'm taking a gap year in South America. I'm outgoing, I love history, and I really enjoy meeting new people.
Interviewer: And how long have you been living in São Paulo?
Danny: For about three months now. I'm staying at a hostel in the city center.
Interviewer: Our tours are in English, but the guides need some Portuguese, too. Do you speak it?
Danny: A little. I've been taking classes since I arrived, so I can have simple conversations. My Portuguese isn't perfect yet, but it's getting better every week.
Interviewer: Do you have any experience working with the public?
Danny: Yes. Last year, I worked at a supermarket in Chicago, so I'm used to dealing with customers. And for the last two months, I've been helping the owner of my hostel. I show new guests around the neighborhood and recommend places to eat.
Interviewer: That's useful. So why do you want to work for City Steps?
Danny: Well, honestly, I really need the money... I mean... I love this city, and I think tourists should see more than the usual places. I'd like to show them the real São Paulo.
Interviewer: OK. You know, our tours are three hours long, on foot, rain or shine, and mostly on weekends. Is that a problem for you?
Danny: Not at all. I've been running with a group in Ibirapuera Park, so I'm in good shape, and I'm free on weekends.
Interviewer: Good. What would you say is your greatest weakness?
Danny: I'm not very organized. I sometimes forget small things. But I've been using a planner app on my phone, and it's really helping.
Interviewer: And how do you deal with difficult customers?
Danny: I try to stay calm and listen to the problem first. At the supermarket, I learned that most people just want someone to listen.
Interviewer: Great. Do you have any questions for me?
Danny: Um, no, I don't think so... Actually, yes! How many people are there in a tour group? And when would I start?
Interviewer: Groups have up to fifteen people, and we need someone from next month. We'll let you know by Friday.
Danny: Perfect. Thank you so much for your time.
